description: We are TERRASAT, building FieldShift, a smart farming advisor powered by NASA POWER satellite data. Our app helps farmers adapt to climate change by analyzing 25 years of temperature, rainfall, humidity and solar trends for any farm location worldwide, then recommending resilient crops, flagging drought and heat risks, and showing health impact assessments. We combine NASA Earth observations with soil data to give actionable farming advice.
summary: FieldShift is a web app that helps farmers compare what they could plant next. Users select a location on an interactive globe or search by city, then explore NASA POWER climate records from 2001–2025 alongside modeled soil conditions. Our Pakistan pilot combines these inputs with crop planting windows and water benchmarks to compare rainfed and irrigated rotations. In Peshawar, the top-ranked rotation changes from sesame followed by chickpea under rainfed conditions to cotton followed by chickpea with irrigation. FieldShift addresses the challenge by turning Earth observation data into a concrete planting decision that growers can review before committing seed, water, and labor.
details:
FieldShift uses NASA POWER monthly climate data to show historical rainfall, temperature, humidity, and solar radiation for a selected location. ISRIC SoilGrids provides modeled surface soil estimates where available. Climate lookup works worldwide where the source data is available. The crop rotation pilot uses Pakistan’s regional crop profiles and planting calendars.

The planner pairs warm-season and cool-season crops, checks whether their planting and harvest windows fit, and compares the results under rainfed and irrigated conditions. In Peshawar, the rainfed setting ranks sesame followed by chickpea first, with a 530 mm combined seasonal crop water benchmark. Under the irrigated setting, cotton followed by chickpea ranks first, with a 930 mm benchmark. Users can compare those options and check local water access and planting dates before picking a sequence.

We built FieldShift with JavaScript, React, Vite, and Tailwind CSS. Three.js and React Globe.gl power the interactive globe, Recharts displays climate history, and jsPDF exports a planning summary. https://drive.google.com/file/d/146ik5Wr6VQ6Rupdh6QMkdyi_zxYyFUoo/view?usp=sharing
